title: Word Bank, Frame, Model
tag: One classroom move, under three minutes, for the teacher who teaches content, not English.

a: Move four
Word Bank, Frame, Model
beats.say: Six Moves, from EL Publishing. Move four: word bank, frame, model.

chunks.text: Six Moves, from EL Publishing. Move four: word bank, frame, model.

a: The prompt
Explain how a plant cell is different from an animal cell.
What comes back
(nothing)
beats.say: You give a writing prompt: explain how a plant cell is different from an animal cell. Your English learners write nothing. Or two sentences. The prompt isn't the problem. The blank page under it is. No vocabulary, no structure, no example — it's the writing equivalent of saying, go talk for five minutes.

a: Three things on the page first
beats.say: The move is three things on the page before anyone writes a word.

chunks.text: The move is three things on the page before anyone writes a word.

a: ① Word bank · cell wall · chloroplast · membrane · nucleus · both · only · unlike
beats.say: One: a word bank. The eight or ten words they'll need, right there on the page. Cell wall, chloroplast, membrane, nucleus, both, only, unlike.

chunks.text: One: a word bank. The eight or ten words they'll need, right there on the page.
Cell wall, chloroplast, membrane, nucleus, both, only, unlike.

a: ② Frame · Both cells have ___. Only a plant cell has ___. Unlike an animal cell, a plant cell ___.
beats.say: Two: a frame, or a structure. Both cells have blank. Only a plant cell has blank. Unlike an animal cell, a plant cell blank. That's a compare paragraph with the grammar already standing up.

chunks.text: Two: a frame, or a structure. Both cells have blank. Only a plant cell has blank.
Unlike an animal cell, a plant cell blank.

a: ③ Model · a paragraph you wrote — about a different topic
beats.say: Three: a model. One paragraph that you wrote, about a different topic — say, a bike and a car — so they can see the shape without copying the content.

chunks.text: Three: a model.

beats.say: Word bank, frame, model. With those three, a level two writes a paragraph. Without them, nobody does.

chunks.text: Word bank, frame, model. With those three, a level two writes a paragraph. Without them, nobody does.

a: What good looks like, by level
Level 1 · labels the diagram, copies 2 frame sentences
Level 2 · 4–5 sentences from the frames
Level 3 · a paragraph from the word bank + structure
Level 4 · paragraph from the model; push connectors
beats.say: And know what good looks like at each level, so you can be happy with it. A level one labels the diagram and copies two frame sentences — that's writing, it counts. A level two gives you four or five sentences from the frames. A level three writes the paragraph from the word bank and the structure. A level four writes from the model alone, and you push on connectors: however, as a result, which means.

a: A level-two paragraph
Both cells have a nucleus.
Both cells have a membrane.
Only a plant cell has a cell wall.
Only a plant cell has chloroplasts.
Unlike an animal cell, a plant cell makes its own food.
beats.say: Here is a level-two paragraph. Both cells have a nucleus. Both cells have a membrane. Only a plant cell has a cell wall. Only a plant cell has chloroplasts. Unlike an animal cell, a plant cell makes its own food. Five sentences, correct science, correct English, from a student who wrote nothing in August. That is a win. Say so.
